Health Connect and Apple Health in Home Assistant or on your own server

Life Dashboard Companion sends what your watch, ring or scale records to a server of your own: Home Assistant, the Grafana stack, MQTT or your own webhook. Every source app at once, with no account and no Google account in between.

  • Android €4.99 once on Google Play: the easy way, with automatic updates, and it supports development. Or free, the same app with the same signing key: the APK on GitHub, Obtainium or F‑Droid.
  • iPhone €6.99 once on the App Store, no subscription. Or build it with Xcode on a Mac with an Apple Developer Program membership.
  • Any brand through the phone, Android and iPhone in one integration
  • All your history in Home Assistant, kept when you change phones
  • Day totals that add up: a walk on phone and watch counts once
  • Edits and deletions are sent too, not only new records
  • Screen time per app next to your health data, on Android
  • Open source (MIT), the same signing key on GitHub, F‑Droid and Google Play

From your watch to your server

Health Connect and Apple Health keep their data on the phone, with no web API. Life Dashboard Companion reads it there on your schedule and sends only what's new.

Samsung Health Apple Watch Google Health Fitbit Pixel Watch Garmin Connect Oura Withings Gadgetbridge Zepp and more

Not every brand shares everything. Samsung and Garmin keep HRV and resting heart rate to themselves, and Garmin Connect needs Android 14. See what arrives for Garmin, Samsung, Fitbit and the other brands.

A Home Assistant integration, paired with one QR code

Installs through the Marketplace (HACS before Home Assistant 2026.11). No YAML, no broker, and the phone never gets a Home Assistant login.

  • Sensors for steps, sleep, heart rate, weight and more
  • All your history in long-term statistics
  • Sleep stages per night, and a card that draws the night
  • Screen time in total and per app, and cards for today, the week and the family
  • An example Health dashboard to copy
More about the integration

{
  "source": "health_connect",

Your own server, database or tool

Any URL that takes JSON: n8n, Node-RED or a script of your own. Or an MQTT broker you already run. Once the data is in your own database, a model on your own network can read it too.

  • Every record in full, signed with HMAC-SHA256 if you set a secret
  • Custom headers and client certificates
  • An outbox that waits for your server
Send Health Connect data to your own webhook

Postgres and Grafana on your own machine

A receiver, Postgres and six Grafana dashboards for both apps, on a home server, a Raspberry Pi or Kubernetes. Its demo shows 60 days of made-up data before you install anything on a phone.

  • One install command, published images, nothing to build
  • Each phone pairs by QR code, as with Home Assistant
  • A read-only API and an MCP server for your own AI
  • A Helm chart, with Postgres from CloudNativePG
More about the Grafana stack

One payload, from Android and iPhone

Both apps send the same JSON, so an Android phone and an iPhone can share one Home Assistant or one stack.

Android34 Health Connect types, screen time per app, and scale readings back into Samsung Health. iPhone28 Apple Health types, with a widget and Shortcuts. On the App Store for €6.99 once, no subscription. Building it yourself with Xcode stays free.

Built for my own dashboard first

I'm Owen Vogelaar. I started this app to feed a personal dashboard of my own, a private project that pulls my health and phone data together in one place. Getting that data off the phone turned out to be the hard part, so the app became a project of its own.

Most people who want this already run Home Assistant, so I built the integration; for anyone who'd rather have plain Postgres and Grafana, the stack. The app runs on my own phone every day.

A good part of the code is written with AI help; the AI policy explains how changes are reviewed and tested. Questions and ideas go to Discussions.

Common questions

Do I need Home Assistant?

No. Home Assistant gets the most out of it, with the integration's sensors and history, but both apps also send to the Grafana stack, to any MQTT broker, and to any URL that accepts a JSON POST, such as n8n, Node-RED or a script of your own. The webhook guide shows the payload.

Can I ask an AI about my data?

Yes, with a model you choose, once the data is on your server. The apps contain no AI and never talk to a model. The Grafana stack has a read-only MCP server, and in Home Assistant a community server, ha-mcp, reads the history. With a local model nothing leaves your network; with a cloud model such as Claude, your questions and the results go to its provider. Health Connect data over MCP has the steps.

Why a separate app instead of the Home Assistant companion app?

Keep the companion app for presence, notifications and device sensors; the two run side by side. Its 36 Health Connect sensors show the latest value or a daily total, with history from the day you enable them. Life Dashboard Companion reads 34 types, keeps every day in long-term statistics, adds screen time per app, and also sends to MQTT and webhooks. The comparison lists the differences.

Which watches, rings and scales work?

Anything that writes to Health Connect or Apple Health: Samsung Health, Apple Watch, Google Health (Fitbit and Pixel Watch), Garmin Connect, Oura, Withings, Gadgetbridge and many more. What arrives depends on what each vendor shares: Garmin and Samsung, for example, don't share HRV or resting heart rate with Health Connect, and Garmin Connect needs Android 14. The brand guides show what each one writes and what it keeps to itself.

What does it cost?

The code of all four parts is MIT licensed and free. On Android, Google Play is the easy way: €4.99 once (US$4.99), no subscription, with automatic updates, and buying it supports development. The free routes stay free: the signed APK on GitHub, Obtainium, which installs that same APK, and F‑Droid. All of them are the same app, built from the same source and signed with the same key. The iPhone app works the same way: building it yourself with Xcode is free, and the App Store version is the paid convenience, €6.99 once (US$5.99), with no subscription.

What do these words mean?

Health Connect is the place on Android where Samsung Health, Garmin Connect and other apps store your health data; Apple Health is the same on iPhone. Home Assistant is open-source software that runs a smart home on a computer in your house. The Marketplace (HACS before Home Assistant 2026.11) is the store for extra Home Assistant integrations. An APK is an Android app file you install yourself, outside the Play Store. A webhook is a web address on your own server that receives data. MQTT is a messaging system many smart homes use. A backfill sends older data, as far back as your phone has it.

Is it a medical device?

No. Life Dashboard Companion moves data your watch, ring or scale already recorded to a server you run. It doesn't measure, diagnose or treat anything and gives no health advice. Talk to a doctor about what the numbers mean for you.

How is it built, and where does AI come in?

I build it with a lot of help from Claude Code, which drafted a large part of the code. I decide what gets built and read every change before it lands. CI runs unit tests, lint and an instrumented suite on an Android emulator, and changes to syncing are tested by hand on a real phone against Home Assistant before a release. The apps contain no AI and call no AI service. The AI policy has the details.

It's one person's project. What if it stops?

Your setup doesn't depend on that person. There's no Life Dashboard server to switch off, your history lives in your own Home Assistant or database, and the MIT license lets anyone carry the code on. The first release shipped in February 2026, and the changelog tracks every change since.

Life Dashboard

Life Dashboard is an open-source project by Owen Vogelaar, in four parts: the Life Dashboard Companion apps for Android and iPhone, a Home Assistant integration and a Grafana stack. It isn't related to other apps or templates called Life Dashboard. Questions go to Discussions.
